title: HTML, CSS & Web Accessibility
description: Modern HTML and CSS reference covering document structure, semantics, links, forms, media, tables, the cascade, selectors, layout, responsive design, container queries, typography, animation, accessibility, performance, and production quality.

subtopics.title: Document Structure & Metadata
subtopics.description: Declare the HTML document, language, UTF-8 early, responsive viewport, unique title, useful description, canonical URL, and only the metadata the page actually supports.

codeBlocks.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Account settings · Example</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Manage profile and security settings.">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/settings">
</head>
<body>...</body>
</html>

callouts.title: Do Not Disable User Zoom
callouts.text: Avoid maximum-scale and user-scalable=no. Users must be able to zoom, and layouts should remain usable at high text and page magnification.

subtopics.title: Landmarks, Sections & Headings
subtopics.description: Use elements by meaning: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer, headings, lists, and paragraphs. Keep a logical heading hierarchy that describes the document.

callouts.title: Choose Native Semantics Before ARIA
callouts.text: Native elements provide roles, states, keyboard behavior, and platform integration. ARIA can supplement missing semantics but does not add behavior automatically.

subtopics.title: Links, Buttons & Navigation
subtopics.description: Links navigate to resources; buttons perform actions. Provide descriptive accessible names and preserve expected keyboard, new-tab, download, and history behavior.

callouts.title: Clickable div Is Not a Button
callouts.text: Adding a click handler does not provide focus, keyboard activation, disabled semantics, form behavior, or accessibility mappings. Use the native control.

subtopics.title: Forms, Labels & Validation
subtopics.description: Associate every control with a visible label, choose the correct type and autocomplete token, group related controls, and connect help and errors programmatically.

callouts.title: Server Validation Is Authoritative
callouts.text: Browser validation improves UX but can be bypassed. Validate and authorize on the server, return field-specific errors, preserve entered values safely, and focus or summarize failures.

subtopics.title: Data Tables
subtopics.description: Use tables for genuinely tabular relationships, with captions and header cells scoped to rows or columns. Keep reading order meaningful and responsive behavior accessible.

callouts.title: Do Not Use Tables for Layout
callouts.text: CSS Grid and Flexbox provide visual layout without introducing false tabular relationships to assistive technology.

subtopics.title: Images, Audio, Video & Embeds
subtopics.description: Provide meaningful alternatives, intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources, captions/transcripts, and lazy loading only below the initial viewport.

callouts.title: Alternative Text Depends on Purpose
callouts.text: Describe the information or function the image contributes. Use empty alt for truly decorative images and do not repeat adjacent text mechanically.

subtopics.title: Cascade, Layers & Specificity
subtopics.description: The cascade resolves origin, importance, layer, specificity, scoping proximity, and source order. Use layers and low-specificity selectors to make overrides predictable.

callouts.title: Avoid Specificity Escalation
callouts.text: Nested IDs, repeated classes, and !important create override arms races. Define layer ownership and component states instead of matching deeper DOM structure.

subtopics.title: Box Model, Flow & Positioning
subtopics.description: Normal flow should do most layout work. Set border-box globally, understand containing blocks and margin behavior, and use positioning when an element intentionally leaves or anchors within flow.

callouts.title: Absolute Positioning Is Not General Layout
callouts.text: Absolute elements do not reserve flow space and often break with localization, zoom, dynamic content, or responsive containers. Use it for intentional overlays and anchors.

subtopics.title: Flexbox, Grid & Intrinsic Sizing
subtopics.description: Use Flexbox for one-dimensional distribution and Grid for two-dimensional tracks. Intrinsic min-content behavior often explains overflow in nested layouts.

callouts.title: Use minmax(0, 1fr) for Shrinkable Content
callouts.text: Grid and flex items have automatic minimum sizes. Explicit zero minimums let intended content areas shrink while overflow is handled locally.

subtopics.title: Media & Container Queries
subtopics.description: Design mobile-first from content needs, use media queries for viewport/user environment, and container queries for components that adapt to their allocated space.

callouts.title: Test Content, Not Device Names
callouts.text: Resize continuously and test long translations, large text, zoom, narrow split-screen windows, touch, pointer, dark mode, forced colors, and reduced motion.

subtopics.title: Focus, Keyboard, Contrast & Motion
subtopics.description: Keep visible focus, logical DOM order, complete keyboard access, sufficient contrast, understandable status messages, and alternatives for motion-sensitive users.

callouts.title: Do Not Reorder Meaning with CSS
callouts.text: Grid/flex order can diverge from reading and keyboard order. Keep DOM order logical and use CSS only for visual arrangement that preserves meaning.

subtopics.title: Performance, Testing & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Keep critical rendering small, reserve media space, avoid expensive layout/paint patterns, validate markup, and combine automated checks with keyboard and assistive-technology testing.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Semantics and heading/landmark structure are logical
□ Forms have labels, instructions and connected errors
□ Keyboard, focus, zoom, text spacing and reduced motion work
□ Layout handles long content and narrow containers
□ Images have dimensions, responsive sources and correct alternatives
□ CSS layers/tokens have clear ownership
□ HTML/CSS validation and accessibility automation pass
□ Real browser, screen reader and performance checks complete

callouts.title: Automation Finds Only Part of Accessibility
callouts.text: Automated tools catch many structural issues but cannot prove clear language, sensible focus, usable keyboard flows, correct alternatives, or a coherent screen-reader experience.
